relevance_note: The paper describes two new patients with Tangier disease ('we have studied two additional patients') and tabulates ten previously reported cases (Table I); no ABCA1 variant is reported for anyone (pre-molecular paper), so the flag is true on the diagnosis criterion.
method_note: Read by hand; a short Python script assembled the rows and checked every span against the paper, with Table I cells sliced from the Markdown rows and checked against the table by eye. Pre-molecular paper (received 1970): no ABCA1 variant or genetic test is reported for anyone, so the variants table is empty; people are in scope on a diagnosis of Tangier disease or as tested relatives. In scope: the paper's two cases (Case 1 = R.W., Case 2 = C.S.), their tested relatives described in the text, and the ten previously reported patients tabulated in Table I rows 1-6 (row 7, 'Bale, Clifton-Bligh, Benjamin, & Whyte.', families 7 8, is this paper's own Case 1 and Case 2 and gets no extra rows). Table I has no label column and four of its rows hold two patients (families 1, 2, 3, 5) with their values stacked in one cell separated by spaces ('M F', '5 7', '+ +'); labels for the second person of such a row add ' 2' ('Table I row 1 2'). Under D-31 none of the stacked values (sex, age, tonsils, splenomegaly, neuropathy, rectal and marrow storage, cornea, plasma and HDL cholesterol) was assigned to either person, including identical pairs such as 'F F' or '0 0'; a single value printed in a two-person row was not assigned either, because row 7 shows single values that belong to one person only (Case 1 had no lipid studies). Only the family number and source reference (single cells) and text statements were used for those people. The schema's older status description allows positional assignment when counts match; the v6 instructions were followed instead. Table I symbols are not defined in a legend: '-' was treated as not reported throughout; '+' was read as present; '±' (row 6 neuropathy) and empty cells as not reported. The Table I 'Age' column is unlabelled; it was recorded as age at diagnosis for the single-person rows 4 and 6 because the text says 'Six patients were diagnosed in childhood, and the other six between 16 and 48 years', which matches the column; this is an interpretation. Table II (relatives' lipoprotein values) is also stacked ('Father Mother Sister Grandfather', 'L.W. H.W. J.W. I.T.', ages and values), so no initials, ages or values were assigned from it; relatives are labelled from the text (Case 1: 'the father and mother', 'The only sibling, a girl', 'the only living grandparent' without stated sex; Case 2: 'Both parents' without stated sex, so 'parent of Case 2' and 'parent of Case 2 2'). Not given rows: Case 1's 'other three grandparents' who died of cardiovascular disease (untested, not affected) and Case 2's maternal grandmother (only a name). OCR garbling: several fractional ages are corrupted ('6ł-year-old', '2† years', '6¢ years', '5♀ years', and 'At the age of 21 years' for Case 1's enlarged tonsils, impossible for a child who died at 5); garbled ages were kept verbatim where used with no ISO conversion, and the '21 years' onset was not recorded. Case 1's age at death comes from 'at death at the age of 5 years'. Case 1 consanguinity recorded 'no' from 'There was no known consanguinity.'; Case 2 left not reported ('no definite knowledge of consanguinity' though the maternal grandmother's maiden name matched). Case 1 is_proband left null (never called propositus); Case 2 is called 'the propositus'. Contradictions / judgement calls: Case 1 skin: 'there were no skin lesions' grossly but 'a few pale macrophages around dermal capillaries and small nerves' on histology; both rows emitted and checklist 'skin lipid deposits' left not reported. Case 1 coronary: 'no lipid streaking of aorta or coronary arteries' but 'focal coronary intimal thickening of uncertain significance'; both rows emitted, 'coronary artery disease' left not reported. Case 1 had a single 'attack of tonsillitis', so 'recurrent tonsillitis or tonsillectomy' is not reported. Case 2 spleen was palpable at 2 and 6 years but 'Neither the spleen nor the liver are palpable' at 15: both rows emitted; checklist splenomegaly observed as a change over time, not a contradiction. Case 2 cornea: 'No abnormalities are to be seen in the cornea' recorded as excluded 'abnormalities in the cornea'; under D-27 this whole-organ statement does not exclude the narrower checklist item 'corneal opacity', left not reported. Case 2 tonsils were removed; 'residual firm yellow tissue' and orange-yellow pharyngeal areas recorded as features, checklist 'orange-colored or enlarged tonsils' left not reported. Case 1 sister: normal plasma cholesterol 'with normal proportions' in the fractions; recorded as excluded low plasma cholesterol only; low HDL left not reported. Table I row 1 (Fredrickson 1961, family 1) vital status 'alive' and the marrow statements come from text naming 'the original two children from Tangier island' / 'The two original cases', tied to family 1 by 'the first of which lived on Tangier Island'. Not assigned for lack of a person-level link: 'The only previously reported patient to die (Hoffman and Fredrickson, 1965) was a man aged 48 years' and 'case 1 of Hoffman and Fredrickson (1965)' with a bleeding disorder (row 3 has two patients); jejunal biopsy and nerve/muscle/skin biopsy statements for the Hoffman and Engel patients. Publications: first author 'Bale' taken from Table I row 7, which lists this paper's two cases (the author line itself is garbled); year not printed (only 'Received for publication 27 November 1970'); n_patients_reported = 2 new patients (no one has an ABCA1 variant reported).
